definition: An ionized state of matter containing free electrons and ions.
do_not_confuse_with: First plasma establishes operation, not fusion gain.

definition: Hydrogen isotope whose nucleus has one proton and one neutron.
do_not_confuse_with: Ordinary hydrogen and tritium.

definition: Radioactive hydrogen isotope with one proton and two neutrons; half-life about 12.3 years.
do_not_confuse_with: An abundant ready-to-use fuel reserve.

definition: Helium-4 nucleus produced in D-T fusion; its charged-particle energy can heat the plasma.
do_not_confuse_with: The neutron, which carries most D-T energy and is not magnetically confined.

definition: Fusion power divided by external heating power delivered across the stated plasma or device boundary.
do_not_confuse_with: Power drawn from the grid; denominator conventions vary and must be disclosed.

definition: Fusion energy from one implosion divided by driver energy delivered to the target.
do_not_confuse_with: Wall-plug electricity, fuel-absorbed energy, or electrical output.

definition: Fusion output divided by energy actually coupled into the fusion fuel under a stated definition.
do_not_confuse_with: Target gain; much driver energy may never reach the fuel.

definition: Energy delivered to the target or plasma divided by electrical input to the driver system.
do_not_confuse_with: Fusion gain; a device can improve one while the other remains low.

definition: For this site only: gross electrical output divided by all recirculating plant electrical consumption over the same complete interval.
do_not_confuse_with: Other authors may call different ratios engineering Q; always display the actual numerator and denominator.

definition: Gross generated electrical energy minus every included plant electrical input, measured over a stated complete cycle or interval.
do_not_confuse_with: Momentary current, capacitor recovery, or gross generation.

definition: Net electrical energy delivered at the grid connection over an interval, accounting for imports and stored-energy changes.
do_not_confuse_with: An isolated pulse or a signed power-purchase agreement.

definition: Fusion-product self-heating becomes sufficient to sustain or propagate the burn under the specified physical criterion.
do_not_confuse_with: A universal synonym for Q greater than 1; physical ignition and target breakeven are distinct.

definition: A plasma substantially heated by its own fusion products, typically with self-heating dominating external heating.
do_not_confuse_with: Continuous commercial electricity generation.

definition: Number density times temperature times energy confinement time, with conventions, units and averaging stated.
do_not_confuse_with: Pulse duration times record temperature from a different experiment.

definition: Characteristic time for stored plasma thermal energy to be lost; commonly W_plasma / P_loss under the stated power balance.
do_not_confuse_with: Total duration of a maintained plasma discharge.

definition: Length of an experimental discharge or specified high-performance interval.
do_not_confuse_with: Energy confinement time or full power-plant availability.

definition: Number of complete shots or pulses per second, measured with specified driver energy and target conditions.
do_not_confuse_with: A one-off maximum shot rate maintained at low power.

definition: A surrounding reactor subsystem that may absorb energy, shield components and breed tritium.
do_not_confuse_with: A demonstrated fuel-self-sufficient plant simply because a blanket is drawn.

definition: Tritium generated divided by tritium consumed under a stated neutronics and accounting boundary.
do_not_confuse_with: Net recoverable surplus after processing losses, decay and inventory needs.

definition: A magnetic-plasma exhaust region that handles escaping heat and particles.
do_not_confuse_with: A blanket; exhaust and neutron-heating loads are different.

definition: A material that remains superconducting at higher temperatures than conventional low-temperature superconductors; fusion magnets still require cryogenic cooling.
do_not_confuse_with: Room-temperature magnets or a guarantee of low overall plant demand.

definition: A compact plasma configuration with magnetic-field reversal in its core and no material center column through the confined region.
do_not_confuse_with: A specific company, fuel or energy-conversion method.

definition: A description for reactions whose main products are charged particles rather than neutrons.
do_not_confuse_with: Zero neutron production, zero radiation, or no shielding in an operating plant.

definition: Fusion power describes nuclear energy release; gross electrical output and net electrical output describe different later boundaries.
do_not_confuse_with: Interchangeable units just because all use MW.
